about: How an Elden Ring enemy's swing becomes a KCD2 zone. The same tracker measures the player's own swings for swing_map.

rows.why: Elden Ring NPC attack animations are a000_003000-003999 (anim id % 1000000); the enemy is attacking from the first frame of such an animation
First bone name found on the character's Havok skeleton wins (player skeleton: 150 bones, R_Weapon #119, seen in game)

Zone = the KCD2 sector containing the screen-plane direction the blade comes FROM (opposite of its motion) at its fastest. Swing lab on the player's straight sword: R1-1 measured upper_right, R1-2 upper_left, matching how they look. The 'cocked position' rule failed (a resting blade hangs low-right, so it always said 'lower')

First sighting of an attack: its zone shows once the blade's screen-plane speed passes this (the strike itself; the lab saw wind-ups at 2-8 m/s and strikes at 13-35 m/s, and slower thresholds fired on the wind-up's direction)
Seconds of each enemy attack tracked; at the end its peak-velocity zone is stored in the learned table
Zones learned per (enemy NpcParam id, animation id). Once an attack is in the table its zone shows from the first frame of the wind-up, like KCD2's incoming-attack marker

Thrust when, over the 0.15 s around the fastest moment, the blade's travel along the camera's view axis exceeds its screen-plane travel by this factor (a slash curves around the body, so the instant velocity alone misjudges it)
A swing whose screen-plane path is shorter than this is a thrust (player) or unknown (enemy: any guard side blocks)
One sample per game frame; velocity is taken over two frames because the pose buffer is double-buffered (alternate frames repeat)
Enemies without a tracked bone (beasts, some bosses): every guard side blocks, and the marker shows all four zones
